correctness.rationale: Complete mapping forces zero fixed; full support has a bijection to m independent \(\operatorname{Sym}(\Lambda)\) choices and n independent \(\operatorname{Sym}(I)\) choices. For one absent P-entry, each left index gives a forbidden event with exact t-fold probability \((n)_t/(mn)^t\). Inclusion-exclusion proves the count; domination by \(1/t!\) proves the joint limit. Brute direct product-map enumeration independently agrees for (m,n)=(2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3); the general result is symbolic, not extrapolated.

evidence: Theorem 6.2 gives balanced-support/Hall equivalence for existence in combinatorial Rees 0-matrix semigroups; Proposition 6.5 counts diagonal-support Brandt semigroups by Latin squares; neither gives a count for one missing support entry.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The existence criterion applies to our support and establishes only positivity, not the exact number or asymptotic ratio. The Brandt count addresses the identity sandwich pattern, not an all-one-minus-one pattern for \(m,n\ge2\). Additional independent enumeration is required; an uninspected classical general enumeration could still dominate.

originality.rationale: The full text of the relevant 2026 source (especially Theorem 6.2 and Proposition 6.5) supplies an existence test for general Rees zero-matrix supports and a Latin-square count for the opposite extreme of diagonal support, but does not state the exact all-one-minus-one enumeration, fixed-dimension limits, or joint \(e^{-1}\) survival law in the inspected relevant sections. The new statements do not follow in value from an existence equivalence or from diagonal Brandt counts. Targeted literature comparisons found no covering statement; this is a qualified self-review originality assessment, not a priority certificate.
residual_risks: A classical rook-polynomial, permanental, or generalized transversal enumeration, perhaps under different terminology, might imply this one-defect formula.

value.rationale: The first natural perturbation of the fully supported combinatorial Rees 0-matrix has an exact all-size complete-mapping enumeration and a counterintuitive macroscopic survival law \(e^{-1}\) from removal of just one support entry. This refines recent existence-only Hall-type Rees criteria quantitatively and gives different fixed-side asymptotics. It is an all-parameter structural count, not a table or arbitrary numeral.
